interface.name: banner_ahb_v1

description.summary: Android gralloc buffers behind dma-buf wl_buffers

interface.description:
Zero-copy window layers on Android. A Vulkan swapchain image that the client allocated as an Android AHardwareBuffer (gralloc) is still shared as a dma-buf through zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1, so the compositor can import and draw it the usual way. This interface additionally hands the compositor the AHardwareBuffer itself, once per wl_buffer, so the compositor can put the buffer straight on an Android SurfaceControl layer (SurfaceFlinger / the display hardware composite it) without copying it.
The AHardwareBuffer travels over a Unix socket: the client creates a socketpair, writes the buffer's handle into one end with AHardwareBuffer_sendHandleToUnixSocket, then sends the other end in the attach request. The compositor reads it with AHardwareBuffer_recvHandleFromUnixSocket and closes the socket. Its reference to the AHardwareBuffer lives as long as the wl_buffer (plus whatever the display still holds).
The compositor advertises this global whenever it can put buffers on a display layer at all; whether it WANTS gralloc buffers right now is the mode event (version 2), sent on bind and every time the user switches zero-copy on or off during the session. A client decides per swapchain, when it creates the swapchain, from the last mode it received, and a client whose live swapchain was built for the other mode retires it (VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR on its next acquire or present) so the program rebuilds it for the new mode. Buffers of the old swapchain stay fully presentable until then: an attached AHardwareBuffer keeps its association for the wl_buffer's lifetime whatever the mode is now. A version 1 client (no mode event) keeps deciding from its own environment. A client that does not see the global (or does not want it) allocates swapchain images the standard way; nothing else changes.
Synchronisation stays implicit: the dma-buf carries the client's render fence (DMA_BUF_IOCTL_IMPORT_SYNC_FILE by the client's driver), the compositor exports it as the layer's acquire fence, and the compositor imports the display's release fence into the dma-buf before it sends wl_buffer.release, so the client's next acquire waits on it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Buffers already attached keep their AHardwareBuffer association.

request.name: attach

description.summary: hand the compositor a buffer's AHardwareBuffer

request.description: Associates the AHardwareBuffer readable from socket with the (already created) dma-buf wl_buffer. width, height and stride (pixels) describe the gralloc allocation; modifier_hi/lo is the DRM format modifier the dma-buf was shared with (the same value passed to zwp_linux_buffer_params_v1.add); image_count is the number of images in the swapchain this buffer belongs to (for the compositor's log). Sent once per wl_buffer, before the buffer is first attached to a surface.

arg.name: socket
arg.summary: socket the AHardwareBuffer handle was written to

arg.name: modifier_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the DRM format modifier

arg.name: modifier_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the DRM format modifier

event.name: mode

description.summary: whether the compositor wants gralloc swapchain images now

event.description: Sent once right after bind and again whenever the compositor's zero-copy state flips (the in-game switch). enabled = 1: swapchains created from now on should use gralloc AHardwareBuffers and attach them; 0: standard buffers. A live swapchain built for the other value should be retired by the client (out of date) so the program rebuilds it; until it is, its buffers are shown as before.

request.name: attach_explicit

description.summary: associate an AHB with explicit fence synchronization

request.description: Experimental fullscreen-only path. Like attach, but accepts a fresh, never-attached android_wlegl wl_buffer without a dma-buf file descriptor. Each new buffer use requires set_acquire_fence or set_acquire_ready before wl_surface.commit. The client must wait on the fenced_release dependency before writing the buffer again. Receipt of wl_buffer.release alone does not mean that dependency has signaled. The association uses this banner_ahb_v1 object for release events; keep it alive until all associated buffers have been retired.

request.name: set_acquire_fence

description.summary: GPU dependency for the next use of this buffer

request.description: fence is a Linux sync_file. This request transfers one descriptor to the compositor; the caller retains ownership of its original descriptor. Only one acquire dependency may be pending per buffer. The buffer must not still be in use by the compositor.

request.name: set_acquire_ready

description.summary: next buffer use has already completed on the producer

request.description: Equivalent to an already-signaled SYNC_FD payload, not permission to omit a dependency for unfinished GPU work.

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: create an AHB-native fullscreen buffer without dma-buf metadata

request.description: The socket carries one AHardwareBuffer handle sent with the public NDK API. Only unprotected single-layer RGBA8 buffers with compositor-overlay usage are accepted. The buffer uses the explicit synchronization rules above. It has no ordinary compositor-copy fallback; use a fullscreen surface without effects or child windows. Clients must retain their original presentation backend for unsupported configurations. This experimental version is advertised only when explicitly enabled.
